equation_request.abstract: We introduce a simple diagrammatic approach for estimating how a randomly walking quantum particle searches on a graph in continuous-time, which involves sketching small weighted graphs with self-loops and considering degenerate perturbation theory’s effects on them. Using this method, we give the first example of degenerate perturbation theory solving search on a graph whose evolution occurs in a subspace whose dimension grows with $N$.

specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk search on a graph with self-loops, H = -gamma*A - |w><w|, simulated by a second-order Trotter product formula on the hypercube (n=2 or 3 qubits) to estimate the marked-vertex success probability. The abstract's diagrammatic degenerate-perturbation-theory method is not reconstructed.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: hypercube Q_n with n=3 (N=8) and a single phase-oracle query per Trotter step. Gamma is scanned numerically, T is near pi*sqrt(N)/2, and the readout is the marked-string probability. Out of scope: the diagrammatic method, the weighted-loop graphs, and the proof of search in a subspace whose dimension grows with N.

symbols.meaning: phase oracle I-2|w><w|, the opaque gate

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Hamiltonian for continuous-time search on a graph with adjacency A; self-loops would add diagonal terms.
equations.justification: Standard CTQW search form (Childs-Goldstone). The abstract names only continuous-time search on graphs with self-loops, not this exact H.
assumptions: The hypercube replaces the paper's weighted loop graphs.
Loop weights are zero in this instance.

equations.label: Oracle step identity
equations.description: Since |w><w|=(I-O_w)/2, the oracle factor is e^{i dt/2} times e^{-i dt O_w/2}. Implementing it with one oracle call needs a controlled-O_w, or an ancilla phase kick built from one oracle call.
equations.justification: Algebra from O_w=I-2|w><w|. The e^{i dt/2} prefactor is a global phase.
assumptions: The placeholder oracle can be controlled by one reserved qubit, giving n+1 qubits total.
The sign of the exponent follows from e^{-iHdt}, which contains e^{+i dt |w><w|}.

equations.label: Second-order Trotter step
equations.latex: U\approx\left(e^{i\gamma A\,dt/2}\,e^{i\,dt|w\rangle\langle w|}\,e^{i\gamma A\,dt/2}\right)^r,\quad e^{i\gamma A\,dt/2}=\bigotimes_i R_X(-\gamma\,dt)
equations.description: Symmetric product formula for e^{-iHT} with T=r dt. The hopping half-step is a layer of RX gates, since RX(theta)=exp(-i theta X/2), so theta=-gamma*dt.
equations.justification: Strang splitting; the X terms commute, so the hopping layer is exact.
assumptions: Trotter error is O(dt^2) and is controlled by large r.

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition, the ground state of -A.

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Marked-string probability, maximized over gamma and T.
equations.justification: The sketch defines success as the marked-vertex probability at an optimal time.
assumptions: gamma is near a critical value, to be found numerically; the 1/N value in the sketch is unverified.

registers.name: v
registers.role: vertex register, little-endian integer encoding (qubit i is bit i of x)

registers.name: a
registers.role: optional ancilla that controls the oracle; return it to |0>

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>, then H on each vertex qubit.

steps.description: Apply H to every vertex qubit to prepare |s>.
Repeat r times: RX layer for half a hopping step, one oracle-phase step with dt, RX layer for half a hopping step.
Measure the vertex qubits only. Read the count of the marked string, taking care with little-endian key order. Scan gamma and T to maximize the probability.

specification.measurement: Measure the n vertex qubits in the computational basis. The marked string is read with qubit 0 as the last character of the counts key. The ancilla is not measured.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_succ from counts, or from the statevector if allowed. Sweep gamma and T and report the peak probability and its time.
assumptions: Hypercube with zero loop weights stands in for the paper's weighted loop graphs.
One oracle query per Trotter step, with a controlled-oracle ancilla.
The Hamiltonian sign convention is H=-gamma*A-|w><w|.
missing_information: The paper's actual graphs and loop weights.
The critical gamma and run time for the paper's graphs.
How the growing-dimension subspace is used.
